subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept the exact `@microsoft/mxc-sdk@0.7.0`/`node-pty` dependency graph and MXC SDK argv-carried config boundary for this official external Windows sandbox plugin after the registration-mode bug is fixed?
rationale: The remaining dependency and process-argv exposure decision is a sandbox/security boundary choice that automation cannot approve, even though the registration-mode bug is mechanically repairable.

options.title: Fix Registration Then Approve Exact Head
options.body: Add the non-full registration guard and test, then have maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and argv boundary for the opt-in external plugin.

options.title: Require A Non-Argv Transport
options.body: Pause the PR until the MXC SDK or OpenClaw provides a config transport that does not expose the encoded sandbox envelope through process argv.

options.title: Defer First-Party MXC Packaging
options.body: Keep MXC outside the official plugin release path until the native dependency and preview SDK boundary are mature enough for maintainer acceptance.

recommendation.title: Fix Registration Then Approve Exact Head
recommendation.body: Add the non-full registration guard and test, then have maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and argv boundary for the opt-in external plugin.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the live assignee and has recent sandbox/OpenShell history, making them the strongest routing owner for the security and release acceptance call.
